title: China AI developers publish safety tests for just 3.6% of model releases, report finds
key_facts: SemiAnalysis, a California research firm, examined 857 model releases between 2021 and 15 Sep 2026 from nine major Chinese AI companies.
The nine were Alibaba, ByteDance, Tencent, Baidu, DeepSeek, Moonshot AI, Z.AI, MiniMax and StepFun.
Model-specific public safety results existed for only 31 releases (3.6%); only nine were available at or before launch.
A disclosure counted only if specific safety results could be tied to an identifiable model.
The study measures transparency, not whether safety work was done; firms may have tested internally without publishing.
Per The420, Reuters reported that China has no broad mandatory rule for frontier developers to publish model-level dangerous-capability tests before release.
quote_evidence: Researchers found published safety results for only 31 releases.
Only nine of the 857 models reviewed had public safety results available at or before the model was released.
Companies may have conducted internal evaluations without publishing the results.
why_it_matters_hint: Outsiders can rarely check Chinese models' safety testing before release, though absence of publication is not absence of testing.
notes: Reuters original blocked (401); TradingView copy is a stub. Facts read in The420.in's account of the SemiAnalysis study and Reuters report; the study itself not read.
